newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Deng family to see patriarch's HK handover triumph.
newsitem.headline: Deng family to see patriarch's HK handover triumph.

text.p: Almost the entire family of the late Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping will come to Hong Kong to celebrate his triumph -- the reunification of the British colony with China, a newspaper said on Thursday.
Deng's eldest son Deng Pufang and daughter Deng Rong will arrive on June 30, the South CHina Morning Post said.
At midnight that day 156 years of British rule over Hong Kong ends and China takes over.
Businessman Deng Zifang, the youngest son, will also come.
"It is believed to be the biggest delegation from the Deng family to Hong Kong," a source told the paper.
Earlier, China announced that Deng's widow Zhuo Lin and daughter Deng Nan would be in the official handover party delegation led by President Jiang Zemin.
Apart from the midnight gala, the family is also expected to join an inauguration ceremony for the new government on July 1.
Deng, who died at 92 in February, opened China to the West, launched economic reforms and pioneered a "one country, two systems" policy under which Britain agreed to hand back Hong Kong.
The territory is to enjoy a high degree of autonomy and no change to its way of life for the next 50 years.
Deng had hoped to be in Hong Kong for the historic sovereignty transfer but his frailty and age foiled his ambition.
